sections.heading: Neural Layer Matrices & Activations Practice Exercises

questions.q: A fully-connected dense layer maps an input \( \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{50} \) to \( \mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^{25} \) using \( \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{W}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b} \). How many total learnable parameters are in this layer?
questions.answer: The weight matrix \( \mathbf{W} \) has shape \( 25 \times 50 \), giving \( 1250 \) weights. The bias vector \( \mathbf{b} \) has \( 25 \) parameters. Total = \( 1250 + 25 = 1275 \).

questions.answer: The weight matrix \( \mathbf{W} \) has shape \( 30 \times 60 \), giving \( 1800 \) weights. The bias vector \( \mathbf{b} \) has \( 30 \) parameters. Total = \( 1800 + 30 = 1830 \).

questions.q: Evaluate the output of the standard ReLU activation function \( f(z) = \max(0, z) \) for inputs \( z_1 = -4 \) and \( z_2 = 6 \).
questions.answer: By definition of the Rectified Linear Unit: \( \text{ReLU}(z) = z \) if \( z > 0 \), and \( 0 \) if \( z \le 0 \). Thus \( f(-4) = 0 \) and \( f(6) = 6 \).

questions.q: The sigmoid activation function is \( \sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}} \). If \( \sigma(z_0) = 0.20 \), what is the value of the derivative \( \sigma'(z_0) \)?
questions.answer: The derivative of sigmoid satisfies \( \sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1 - \sigma(z)) \). Substituting \( \sigma(z_0) = 0.20 \): \( \sigma'(z_0) = (0.20)(1 - 0.20) = (0.20)(0.80) = 0.1600 \).
